style: instrumental video game background music, seamless 90 second loop, the tense variant of a cozy work theme — same room, but the money has run out. In the game a starving startup has weeks to live; the walls know. Mood: uneasy, ticking, holding-your-breath suspense played quiet and dry, never horror. Same half-time skeleton as a calm work loop but hollowed out: sparse felt piano chords with the warmth removed, a single repeated bass note pulsing like a countdown, dry marimba ticking like a wall clock, whisper brushed drums, a low quiet synth drone underneath, and once per phrase one worried, bending muted trumpet note. Lots of negative space; the tension never resolves — the loop ends leaning forward into the next bar. Restrained, intimate, modern small-room production, made to crossfade with its calm sibling. 96 BPM, D minor. No vocals, no strings melodrama, no horror drones, no percussion buildups, no intro, no outro, no fade-out.
